heading: Read a partner’s K-1 alongside the ownership and basis records
body:
A partnership return reports important information, but it is not the entire ownership file. A partner needs to understand the agreement, how the interest was acquired, contributions and distributions, and the basis records maintained for that particular partner. The IRS explains that a capital account shown in the partnership’s books is not the same thing as the adjusted basis of a partnership interest.

Keep three questions separate

First, what economic rights does the agreement provide? Second, what amounts does the partnership report? Third, what partner-level basis and limitations apply? Treating these as one number can produce a misleading answer when a partner buys an interest, assumes a share of liabilities, receives property, or changes ownership during the year.

For a fictional new partner, a purchase payment to an existing partner may not appear as a cash contribution to the partnership. The buyer should preserve the purchase agreement and payment evidence, identify the acquisition date, and ask the preparer what additional schedules or elections need review. Do not recreate purchase basis from the ending capital account alone.

Prepare the adviser’s question list

Bring current and prior K-1s, relevant agreement amendments, transfer documents, contribution and distribution records, liability information, and existing outside-basis schedules. Flag changes in ownership and transactions with related parties. Assign responsibility for reconciling differences between the partnership’s data and the partner’s permanent records.

Read the IRS partner instructions for Schedule K-1 for the applicable year. Use this publication to frame a precise discussion about the records and calculations, rather than assuming a positive capital balance establishes that a proposed loss or distribution has no tax consequences.

Choose the record that matches the partner-level question

Use the capital-and-outside-basis reconciliation guide when preparing the entity-to-partner handoff. Put the K-1, permanent partner records, and unresolved reconciliation questions in the same review file. If refinancing and a proposed cash payment are involved, continue with the refinance-distribution review guide before treating a cash amount as a completed tax conclusion. Record the transaction dates and documents the adviser still needs rather than substituting a general example for the actual transaction.
